title: External Hom; the $\beta$ map
statement:
For $i=1,2$, let $E_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$ and $L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$ on separated finite-type $X_i$, with the
admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] where $!$-pullbacks
occur. The evaluation-defined comparison of [def-sf-kv-maps] (iii)

$$
\beta:\RHom_A(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\RHom_A(E_2,L_2)
\longrightarrow
\RHom_A\bigl(E_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}E_2,\,
L_1\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}L_2\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in all four variables.

proof.text: Fix $L_1,L_2$. For fixed $E_2$, let $\mathcal T_1(E_2)$ be the objects $E_1$ for which the specified $\beta$ is invertible. The two sides are contravariant exact functors in $E_1$, and likewise in $E_2$: on the resolution models of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], tensor with a fixed K-flat complex carries a mapping cone to the mapping cone of the tensored map, and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(-,I)$ carries a cone to the corresponding shifted cone. The evaluation maps defining $\beta$ in [def-sf-kv-maps] respect these cone and shift identifications, using the tensor symmetry with its Koszul signs. All values remain in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Thus [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three], applied on the opposite triangulated category, gives cone closure of $\mathcal T_1(E_2)$. It contains zero and is closed under shifts and finite sums. It is closed under direct summands: if $E_1$ is a retract of $E'_1$, naturality makes $\beta(E_1,E_2)$ a retract in the arrow category of $\beta(E'_1,E_2)$; composing the retraction and section with the inverse gives its inverse. Consequently it is thick. For fixed $E_1$, the two functors in $E_2$ are again contravariant exact by the displayed cone models and $\beta$ respects shifts. Applying [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] gives cone closure in $E_2$; zero, shifts and finite sums are preserved, and a retraction in $E_2$ gives a retraction of the two arrows by naturality. If $s_A,r_A,s_B,r_B$ are the resulting sections and retractions of source and target and $b$ is the invertible larger arrow, $r_A b^{-1}s_B$ is an inverse of the retract arrow, as follows by naturality and $r_As_A=r_Bs_B=1$. Thus this class in $E_2$ is thick too. By [lem-trf-devissage-generation] it is therefore enough to prove $\beta$ for every pair of generators $E_i=Rg_{i*}j_{i!}F_i$. Explicitly, first fix a generator $E_2$ and extend from generator $E_1$ to all $E_1$; then fix any $E_1$ and extend from generator $E_2$ to all $E_2$. This is thick generation, not replacement of lisse sheaves by constant sheaves.

source.place: first paragraph: exactness and dévissage in both $E_i$

proof.text: For these generators write $h_i=g_i\circ j_i:U_i\to X_i$. Here $g_i:\overline U_i\hookrightarrow X_i$ is closed, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and $j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow\overline U_i$ is open. This is a compactification of $h_i$; the defining compactification formula [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] gives $E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i$ without assuming $h_i$ proper. The ring $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite local by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The lisse constructible $F_i$ of [lem-trf-devissage-generation] has finite stalks by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and is locally constant; hence it is locally a finite constant $A$-module with flat stalks. Each such module is free by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free], and its rank is finite because the module is finite. Thus $F_i$ is locally finite free, a site-perfect object concentrated in degree zero. Put $F_i^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_A(F_i,A_{U_i})$ and $C_i=F_i^\vee\otimes_A^L h_i^!L_i$. The exceptional inverse image here is the constructible one of [def-trf-admissibility]; in particular $h_i^!L_i$ is in $D^b_{ctf}(U_i,A)$. The dual $F_i^\vee$ is locally finite free too, and tensor and ordinary direct-image preservation in [thm-sf-ctf-stability] give $C_i\in D^b_{ctf}(U_i,A)$ and $Rh_{i*}C_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,A)$.

source.place: first paragraph: $h_i=g_i j_i$, finite flat stalks, and locally finite-free $F_i$

proof.text:
Apply [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] to the locally finite-free $F_i$ and [lem-sf-tensor-hom] to $(h_i,F_i,L_i)$. Their canonical isomorphisms give
$$
H_i:=R\mathcal Hom_A(E_i,L_i)\simeq Rh_{i*}R\mathcal Hom_A(F_i,h_i^!L_i)\simeq Rh_{i*}C_i.
$$
Set $h=h_1\times h_2$, $F=F_1\boxtimes_A^L F_2$, and $L=L_1\boxtimes_A^L L_2$. Tensoring local finite-free bases makes $F$ locally finite free and identifies its evaluation dual with $F_1^\vee\boxtimes_A^L F_2^\vee$: on a trivializing cover the pairing sends $(\lambda_1\otimes\lambda_2)\otimes(v_1\otimes v_2)$ to $\lambda_1(v_1)\lambda_2(v_2)$, and changes of bases preserve this pairing. Clause (i) of [def-sf-kv-maps], with its isomorphism provided by [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] over $X_1\times X_2$, identifies $E:=E_1\boxtimes_A^L E_2$ with $Rh_!F$. Thus the same tensor–Hom and perfect-evaluation isomorphisms identify
$$
R\mathcal Hom_A(E,L)\simeq Rh_*\bigl(F^\vee\otimes_A^L h^!L\bigr).
$$
All objects to which these statements are applied are in their finite-Tor constructible domains by Step 2 and [thm-sf-ctf-stability]; $h$ is again separated finite type and has the constructible exceptional adjoint.

source.place: first displayed formula and second paragraph: dual of $F$ and the $!$-Künneth identification

proof.text:
The ordinary Künneth map [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth] is used twice, with its actual finite-Tor hypotheses. First use $f=h_1$, auxiliary scheme $X_2$, and auxiliary object $Rh_{2*}C_2$, which is allowed by Step 2. Next use $f=h_2$, auxiliary scheme $U_1$, and object $C_1$, exchanging the two factors. Applying $R(h_1\times\operatorname{id}_{X_2})_*$ to this second isomorphism and using the ordinary composition isomorphism [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] gives the isomorphism
$$
\begin{aligned}
H_1\boxtimes_A^L H_2
&\simeq Rh_{1*}C_1\boxtimes_A^L Rh_{2*}C_2\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}R(h_1\times\operatorname{id}_{X_2})_*(C_1\boxtimes_A^L Rh_{2*}C_2)\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}R(h_1\times\operatorname{id}_{X_2})_*R(\operatorname{id}_{U_1}\times h_2)_*(C_1\boxtimes_A^L C_2)\\
&\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*(C_1\boxtimes_A^L C_2).
\end{aligned}
$$
Denote this composite by $K_*$. The finite-level clause of the composition theorem applies on the pro-étale derived categories; no integral or common-stage coefficient passage is involved.

source.place: second paragraph, first displayed arrow: ordinary Künneth twice

proof.text:
Distribute the external tensors and use the dual pairing from Step 3 to identify
$$
C_1\boxtimes_A^L C_2\simeq F^\vee\otimes_A^L(h_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^L h_2^!L_2).
$$
The exceptional comparison [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth] for $(h_1,h_2,L_1,L_2)$ is an isomorphism
$\alpha_h:h_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^L h_2^!L_2\to h^!L$.
Tensor it with $F^\vee$, apply $Rh_*$, and compose with $K_*$ and the inverse of the target identification in Step 3. This produces an isomorphism
$$
\gamma:H_1\boxtimes_A^L H_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(E,L).
$$
Here the admissibility used is precisely that of the constructible exceptional adjoints in Step 2, not an ambient exceptional-adjoint datum.

We verify that $\gamma$ is the specified evaluation-defined $\beta$, rather than just an unspecified isomorphism. Let $q_i:h_i^*H_i\to C_i$ be the ordinary counit after $H_i\simeq Rh_{i*}C_i$, using the ordinary adjunction in [fix-prop-adjunctions] (1); put $e_i:F_i\otimes_A^L C_i\to h_i^!L_i$ for the perfect-evaluation pairing, and $\mu_i:Rh_{i!}h_i^!L_i\to L_i$ for the constructible exceptional counit in [def-trf-admissibility]. The canonical tensor–Hom isomorphism [lem-sf-tensor-hom] says, on transposing, that evaluation $E_i\otimes_A^L H_i\to L_i$ is
$$
E_i\otimes_A^L H_i\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{h_i}}
Rh_{i!}(F_i\otimes_A^L h_i^*H_i)
\xrightarrow{Rh_{i!}(e_i\circ(1\otimes q_i))}
Rh_{i!}h_i^!L_i\xrightarrow{\mu_i}L_i.
$$
The projection maps here are the natural isomorphisms of [fix-prop-projection-formula]; their second arguments $H_i$ have finite Tor amplitude by Step 2. By the definition of the canonical ordinary comparison, the ordinary transpose of $K_*$ is $q_1\boxtimes q_2$, under $h^*(H_1\boxtimes H_2)=h_1^*H_1\boxtimes h_2^*H_2$. By [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii), the exceptional transpose of $\alpha_h$ is $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ followed by $\mu_1\boxtimes\mu_2$. Consequently, transposing $\gamma$ first across tensor–Hom and then across the ordinary and exceptional adjunctions gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
E\otimes_A^L(H_1\boxtimes_A^L H_2)
&\longrightarrow Rh_!\bigl(F\otimes_A^L h^*(H_1\boxtimes_A^L H_2)\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rh_!((e_1\boxtimes e_2)\circ(1\otimes(q_1\boxtimes q_2)))}
Rh_!(h_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^L h_2^!L_2)\\
&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ku}_!}Rh_{1!}h_1^!L_1\boxtimes_A^L Rh_{2!}h_2^!L_2
\xrightarrow{\mu_1\boxtimes\mu_2}L.
\end{aligned}
$$
The first arrow is the compact-support projection map, after $E\simeq Rh_!F$. The canonical $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ is the composite of base-change and projection maps in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]. The symmetry, iterated-product, base-change and identity-factor projection-formula clauses (i)–(iv) of [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] give the compatibility used here: pull the factor maps to $X_1\times X_2$, insert $H_1,H_2$ as identity-map factors, and regroup the four factors as $(F_1,H_1)$ and $(F_2,H_2)$. Using these clauses, the displayed composite is the external product of the two preceding formulas for evaluation, with only the tensor symmetry moving $H_1$ past $E_2$. It is therefore exactly the tensor–Hom transpose defining $\beta$ in [def-sf-kv-maps] (iii). Injectivity of the adjunction bijections gives $\gamma=\beta$. Hence $\beta$ is invertible for generators, and Step 1 proves it for all $E_i$. Finally, evaluation, tensor symmetry and tensor–Hom transposition are natural (contravariantly in $E_i$, covariantly in $L_i$), so the specified isomorphism is natural in all four variables, independent of the generator choices.

source.place: last sentences: ordinary and exceptional adjoints, evaluation, and the projection formula

split_report.summary: Audited and replaced the earlier sandbox attempt. Kept the source statement and six-functors unit route. Expanded to six proof steps with explicit thick-generation closure, compactification and locally finite-free checks, source/target Hom identifications, two typed ordinary Künneth applications, exceptional Künneth, and the evaluation transpose calculation. Reused existing nodes only; corrected the claim about the Lean structure projection, which is not an unconditional proof and states only existence of some isomorphism. Repeated real Mathlib searches through msearch.py and read the candidate files.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–2 realize the first proof paragraph through the locally finite-free reduction; Step 3 realizes its tensor–Hom formula and the second paragraph’s F-dual and shriek-product identifications; Steps 4–5 realize the two displayed comparison arrows; Step 6 expands the final evaluation/mate calculation.

All 21 cited nodes lie on the transitive route of sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier, so no tool use is needed, and no SGA source is cited. STEPS: (1) lem-trf-devissage-generation gives thick generation in D(X,A); lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three has its exactness and shift hypotheses checked on the K-flat/K-injective models; the retract inverse r_A b^-1 s_B holds in both directions. (2) The generator closed immersion is proper (lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper), so def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed gives E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i. A_{E,n} is finite local (def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension item 4); stalks are finite (def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility) and free (lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free). h^! preserves D^b_ctf by def-trf-admissibility, tensor and Rf_* by thm-sf-ctf-stability (ii)/(iii). (3) prop-sf-dualizable-hom applies to the site-perfect F_i only; lem-sf-tensor-hom (blueprint_update read) and def-sf-kv-maps (i) give E=Rh_!F. (4) lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth is applied twice, with (h_1,X_2,Rh_{2*}C_2) and (h_2,U_1,C_2,C_1) swapped, composed by lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition (1). (5) prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth applies to (h_1,h_2,L_1,L_2). (6) Unwinding the Yoneda chain of lem-sf-tensor-hom gives mu, then adjoint, then PF, in the stated PF direction. The ordinary comparison's adjoint is counit times identity, giving q_1 times q_2 with the composite counit of fix-prop-adjunctions (3). alpha's transpose comes from def-sf-kv-maps (ii); Ku_!/PF coherence comes from lem-sf-kunneth-coherence (i)-(iv). So gamma equals beta. Minor, unchanged: step 6 names fix-prop-adjunctions (1) where clause (3) is also used, but the node cited is correct.
